'''William Earl Moore''' (1941 - 10 December 2020) was an American chemist.  He was the first [[African Americans|African American]] to graduate from [[Purdue University]] with a PhD in chemistry. Moore was a faculty member at [[Southern University]] for more than three decades.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web  |date=2020-12-11 |title=Longtime Southern University faculty member, administrator William Moore dies |url=http://www.subr.edu/news/longtime-southern-university-faculty-member-administrator-william-moore-dies |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=Southern University and A&M College |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Moore was born in born in [[Tuscaloosa, Alabama]], in 1941.<ref>MSO 1, Purdue University Archives and Special Collections Oral History Program collection, Purdue University Archives and Special Collections, Purdue University Libraries. https://archives.lib.purdue.edu/agents/people/2717</ref>

Moore attended [[Southern University]] in [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana]], for his undergraduate studies. He completed his bachelor's degree in chemistry there in 1963.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=William Moore - College of Science - Purdue University |url=https://www.purdue.edu/science/Alumni/recognition/2010-distinguished-science-alumni/william-moore.html |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=www.purdue.edu}}</ref> In 1967, Moore received a PhD in physical biochemistry from [[Purdue University]], making him the first Black person to do so in the history of the university.

His PhD thesis was titled "The Effects of Reversible Denaturation on the Population Distribution of Bovine Serum Albumin" and was submitted in August 1967. His doctoral advisor was Joseph F. Foster, and Moore also thanked Dr. Vandon E. White in his acknowledgements.<ref>{{cite thesis |id={{ProQuest|302252238}} |last1=Moore |first1=William Earl |date=1967 |title=The Effect Of Reversible Denaturation On The Population Distribution Of Bovine Serum Albumin }}{{psc|date=February 2024}}</ref> White was chair of the department of chemistry at [[Southern University]], and has been lauded for his work supporting Black students pursuing graduate studies in chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Vandon E. White Award |url=https://foundation.sus.edu/vandon-e-white-award/ |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=Southern University System Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> Moore also began his thesis with a quotation from [[Bertrand Russell]]. 

== Career ==
In the late 1960s, Moore joined the faculty of [[Southern University]], his alma mater where he had completed his undergraduate studies. Within five years, Moore achieved the rank of full professor.<ref name=":1"/>

In 1973, Moore became the first president of [[Southern University]]'s faculty senate. While at Southern, in 1975, Moore took a yearlong absence to consult 34 [[Historically black colleges and universities|historically Black colleges and universities]] on developing programs in interdisciplinary studies. In 1981, he served as chairman of the General Research Support Review Committee at the [[National Institutes of Health]].<ref name=":1" />

A year later, in 1982, Moore was hired as academic vice president, Distinguished Professor of Chemistry, and director of Title III programs at [[Prairie View A&M University]] in [[Prairie View, Texas]]. In 1985 he left Prairie View to take on the role as academic vice president and chief academic officer at [[Texas Southern University]] in [[Houston|Houston, Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2020-12-22 |title=In Memoriam: William E. Moore, 1941-2020 |url=https://www.jbhe.com/2020/12/in-memoriam-william-e-moore-1941-2020/ |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=The Journal of Blacks in Higher Education}}</ref>

In 1989, Moore returned to [[Southern University]] as vice chancellor for academic affairs.

== Personal life ==
William Moore was married to Willa Moore, who worked at [[Lafayette Home Hospital]] while Moore was a grad student at Purdue.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=In Memoriam: Alumnus Dr. William E. Moore - Purdue University Department of Chemistry |url=https://www.chem.purdue.edu/media/news/2020/moore_obit.html |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=www.chem.purdue.edu}}</ref> They had two children.<ref>{{Cite web |title=William Moore Obituary (2020) - Baton Rouge, LA - The Advocate |url=https://obits.theadvocate.com/us/obituaries/theadvocate/name/william-moore-obituary?id=6859179 |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
In 2006, the Purdue Board of Trustees established the William E. Moore Distinguished Professor of Earth and Atmospheric Science and Chemistry and named [[Joseph Francisco|Joseph S. Francisco]] as the first to hold this appointment.<ref name=":0" /> Other awards include:

* Invited lecture at the [[Pasteur Institute]] in Paris, France (1978)<ref name=":2" />
* Outstanding alumni, Purdue University (2004)
* Distinguished alumni, College of Science, Purdue University (2010)
* Honoree for distinguished commitment and service, Southern University Alumni Federation (2014)<ref name=":1" />
